item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking Neural Networks, or SNNs, are neural networks that communicate with discrete spike events instead of continuously passing dense activation values from layer to layer.

item.title: Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking Neural Networks connects Topic Overview with 1.

item.title: 3.1 Energy Consumption
item.description: Energy Consumption Once spike count and synaptic operations are measurable, energy becomes a quantity you can build from counts instead of a vague claim about a model being “efficient.” Imagine a small vision sensor watching a hallway.

item.title: 3.2 Normalized Energy Efficiency
item.description: After measuring accuracy as “how often the model is right” and energy consumption as “how much work the model spends to make one inference,” the natural question is how to compare them at the same time.

item.title: 3.3 Convergence Time
item.description: After measuring what an SNN spends during inference, the next question is how soon it becomes useful while it is still learning.

item.title: 4.1 How SNNs Learn
item.description: How SNNs Learn Imagine the spiking neuron you have already met sitting inside a small network that watches a changing signal, such as a gesture from an event camera or a short sound pattern.

item.title: 4.2 Surrogate Gradient Training
item.description: Surrogate Gradient Training After learning that an SNN communicates through spike events, the training problem becomes sharper: a neuron can build up internal voltage smoothly for a while, but its outward message is a sudden yes-or-no event.

item.title: 4.3 ANN-to-SNN Conversion
item.description: ANN-to-SNN Conversion You already have the ingredients needed to understand a converted spiking network: an ANN computes with continuous activation values, an SNN communicates with spike trains, and a simulation window gives the spiking network time to express information through events.
